title: Pointwise rank is constant on a free rational-cokernel cover
statement: Let a:R_X^n→R_X^t be an integral finite-free matrix. If scalar extension of coker(a) is pro-etale locally finite free, there is a pro-etale cover V→X such that the E-valued matrix of its normalized integral pullback, in the canonical coordinates [def-weil-pbc-integral-matrix-analytic-data], has the same rank at every pair of points of each member.

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: Choose the supplied cover and a basis of rank q for the rational cokernel on each member. Obtain the coefficient-transport functor, its regular-module comparison, and its free-cokernel comparison.

At each point choose an algebraic closure of its residue field. Lift E to ULift E in the scheme universe, apply compatible geometric-field evaluation, then restrict scalars back along the lift ring equivalence. Transport along the explicit pointwise continuous-function ring isomorphism. The resulting functor is additive, preserves finite colimits, sends the regular continuous coefficient module to E, and evaluates every regular endomorphism at the chosen point.

Compose coefficient transport with evaluation. Use the existing, universe-generalized finiteFreeEvaluationCoords and finiteFreeEvaluationCoords_matrix API in the corank module. The existing matrix_coefficient_pullback theorem identifies each integral pullback coefficient with the original coefficient at the image point.

Preservation of cokernels and the transported free cokernel basis give cokernel dimension q. Use the existing, universe-generalized finrank_cokernel_of_matrix lemma in the corank module to obtain t minus matrix rank equals q. Since matrix rank is at most t, this determines the rank uniquely at every point on the cover member. Zero ranks and empty members need no extra hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.8, continuous coefficient framework, and geometric-field evaluation; scalar coefficient transport followed by ordinary finite-dimensional rank-nullity
proof_origin.note: E4 proves the evaluation and linear-algebra part, including the universe lift for the small coefficient field, and proves the coefficient-transport theorem in the same delivery. Existing coordinate, cokernel-dimension and matrix-pullback lemmas are reused, with their original APIs generalized or exposed in place. No local sorry remains; the original target statement is unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem integralMatrix_pointwise_rank (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (E : Type) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    (n t : ℕ) (X : Scheme.{u})
    (a : Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) n ⟶
      Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) t)
    (hC : ∃ V : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X, ∀ k,
      Mod.IsFree ((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (V.f k)).obj
          (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X))
        (((ProEtale.upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (V.f k)).mapMod _).obj
          ((Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).obj
            (cokernel a)))) :
    ∃ V : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X, ∀ k (x y : V.X k),
      Matrix.rank (fun i j ↦ (integralMatrixPullbackFunctions ℓ E (V.f k) a i j x).val) =
        Matrix.rank (fun i j ↦ (integralMatrixPullbackFunctions ℓ E (V.f k) a i j y).val)
